name: 1836 Calumet Avenue — Brick dwelling (district draft; refined by T-1946)

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-3008 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 27.000, v -7.500 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's own georeference: 0.34 m RMS on its control crossings and 1.47 m RMS on independent standing houses (data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_28_gcps.json), plus about a pixel (0.05 m) of trace. Rotation -0.556 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 1836 S. Calumet Avenue, parcel calumet_1836 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Calumet Avenue, the background behind Prairie Avenue: Calumet Avenue's west frontage, 18th to 20th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 28).

footprint.note: The main body: the largest rectangle that fits inside the traced main part (u toward the street, v along the front). The building's other rectangles are in draft_plan.

stories.note: '2B' printed on the 1911 sheet: 2 full storeys.

construction.note: The register reads the map's colours as 'brick'.

draft_plan.note: Rectangles fitted inside the traced parts by the rules' fit (cell 0.25 m, at most 3 a part, to 90% cover): s28xfp-calumet_1836-b1 p2 (main, brick), rectangle 1 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 90% of its fill; s28xfp-calumet_1836-b1 p2 (main, brick), rectangle 2 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 90% of its fill; s28xfp-calumet_1836-b1 p1 (range, frame), rectangle 1 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 69% of its fill. Roles: the main part's largest rectangle is the main body; a shallow rectangle at the front is a bay; the sheet's ranges, porches and stone fronts keep their roles. Storeys per piece and roof per piece are the draft rules' (reconstructed).

draft_elevation.note: RECONSTRUCTED by the draft rules, family row '(default)' overlaid with the frontage row: A background house with no named record and no register row: the brick family's hip over the sheet's printed storeys, every face closed, nothing read beyond the sheet. An L plan; the sheet's frame front porch is the refining ticket's. Heights are the rules' starting values inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's ranges; bays, entrance side, chimneys and dormers are counts the family rules choose, and the seed 4233956519 only tints the fabric inside +-6 %. Liberty L-draft-district-background-3008.

draft.note: The draft's own provenance: the pass that wrote it, the rows it read and the tickets that replace it attribute by attribute under this id.

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '2B brick dwelling (D) on an L plan, a 2-storey frame porch (yellow) along its Calumet front'. Carried to 1904 on the T-3008 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 28.
what_it_supplies: The water's edge beside the Illinois Central from about 40 m north of 18th Street to about 80 m south of it, and the easternmost track on to the paper's edge, as of 1911
The 1800 Prairie lot and the Glessner House footprint (stone, courtyard plan) as of 1911, and every Prairie- and Calumet-facing footprint from 18th to 20th Street
Its own printed Scale of Feet
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-3008, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-1946 refines in place under this same id. Written by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py from the sheet 28x trace (s28xfp-calumet_1836-b1), the T-3008 census (s28x-1836-front) and the T-1837 register row frontage-28x-1836 (Brick dwelling); every height, roof, opening and feature is the draft rules' reconstruction (data/components/prairie_1904/draft_prairie_1904.json; liberty L-draft-district-background-3008).
